newsitem.title: POLAND: Budimex sees PLN 22 mln net in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Budimex sees PLN 22 mln net in 1996.

text.p: The Polish construction firm Budimex SA expects to make a net profit this year of at least 22 million zlotys, its profit last year, the daily Gazeta Wyborcza reported on Wednesday.

The paper quoted Budimex President Grzegorz Tuderek, who at a meeting with investors in the southern city of Katowice said his firm saw demand in infrastructure projects such as motorways and petrol stations, and residential construction.
"Budimex is counting on a boom in apartment building construction -- in our country there's a lack of 700,000 flats," Wyborcza quoted Tuderek at saying.
Tuderek said this year's earnings were hurt by exceedingly cold weather over the first four months but that a rebound was in store as long as October stayed relatively warm.
The firm earned 13 million zlotys in the first eight months this year against 13.8 million in the same period in 1995.
Tuderek said Budimex -- which has 40 firms in its holding, 15 of them construction firms -- plans to record annual turnovers in the billions of zlotys in two to three years.
It expects sales of 285 million zlotys this year against 274 million zlotys last year, and a pre-tax profit of 33 million zlotys, 43 million for the group.

Tuderek said the company planned in two to three years to lift its percentage of contracts in Poland to half from the current third. The company currently does 40 percent of its work in Germany and 20 percent in Russia.
He said the company planned no new share issue next year.
